inline_text:
A maintenance pass over the whole skills library. Six commits, each
readable on its own.

## The one to look at first

The worked example in `aaif-community-pulse` had been pasted from a real
posted update and named real organizers, in a public repo. It is replaced
with the synthetic cast the other content skills use. The Luma links in it
are public pages and stay, per Rahul.

Nobody needs to act on this beyond the fix — but it is worth knowing the
old commit is still served at its SHA.

## Three duplications resolved, for three different reasons

Not all duplication here is the same, and the repo already knew that.
`AGENTS.md` says a skill script duplicating a helper is deliberate, because
importing `lib/aaif_events` costs the skill its ability to run zipped for
claude.ai. So each of these was decided separately:

**`redact.py` — could not be allowed to differ.** Nine scripts carried
their own copy of `--redact`'s flag and helpers. The duplication was itself
a fix: an earlier refactor moved `redact_email` out but left `REDACT`
behind, so the flag was set in one module and read in another, `--redact`
governed nothing, and an address reached a public CI log. That bug is a
property of *splitting* the flag from the helpers, not of sharing them — so
they now live in one module, and `check_no_local_redaction.py` keeps them
there. The nine copies had already started to drift: one had lost its
address masker.

**`gws.py` and `sheets.py` — had already drifted, invisibly.** Four `gws`
wrappers: two near-identical full ones, two with no retry handling at all.
The two full ones disagreed about whether `Internal error` was retryable,
so whether a run survived a sick API depended on which script you were in.
The two header-lookup copies had made *different* safety choices — one
guarded a non-string cell, the other raised; one aborted on a duplicated
header, the other silently took the first. The safer half of each survives,
which means `sync_chapters` gains a duplicate-header abort it never had.

Scoped to skills already coupled to `lib`. The deliberately standalone ones
keep their own wrappers and stay portable, and
`check_portable_skills.py` now makes that a decision someone records rather
than one that happens an import at a time.

**The `SKILL.md` banners — must be duplicated, so they are pinned.** Skills
ship downstream without the repo docs, so the rules travel inside each
file. The tooling rule has had a drift guard since it was written. The
public-copy rule and the legal footer did not, and existed as nine and four
hand-written variants. All three are now enforced byte-identical.

## Bugs found along the way

- **Retries on a permanent error.** Both `gws` copies excluded only an
  adjacent *digit* from the HTTP-status match, under a comment claiming
  `A500:K500 exceeds grid limits` was handled. It was not — that `500` is
  preceded by `A` and followed by `:`, so a permanent grid-limit error
  burned the full backoff before failing anyway.
- **Seven sheet reads truncated the newest column.** A hardcoded right edge
  drops the most recently added column first, and the layout check then
  aborts naming a column visibly present on the sheet. The same cap was
  copied across two skills.
- **`resolve_slack_ids.py --apply` wrote without `--write`**, so whether an
  invocation writes could not be answered by reading the command line.
- **Two dead imports that read as guarantees.** Two scripts imported an
  address masker they never call. The tests now pin its absence.
- **Three skills missing from the README's standalone-zip caveat**, so
  zipping one would have failed at import. Also: 18 skills where there are
  20, and the legal-footer note naming three skills where four carry it.

## Structure

`aaif-sync-chapters` sheds 300 lines of naming history and applied-migration
prose into `references/`, and its four completed one-shots move from
`scripts/` to `migrations/`. **Moved, not deleted** — the audit that
prompted this called them dead weight, and they are not: two live engines
name one of them as the fix when a sheet is missing its columns, and two
tests cross-check its constants. CI runs their tests from the new location.

`aaif-audit-slack` moves its sheet-schema spec the same way. Both frontmatter
descriptions were over 800 characters on one line — the field that decides
whether a skill activates at all.

## Tests

`audit_members.py` and `audit_activity.py` are durable code feeding a
leadership-facing report and had no tests between them. They now cover the
refusals: the directory cross-check that rejects a short user pull, the
histogram guards, and the cache rules — a 90-day count under a 30-day
headline is a wrong number that looks fully measured.

The Verify list named 12 tests where 15 existed, omitting the one for
`provision_channels.py`, the most dangerous script in the skill. A test now
fails if it drifts again.

## The missing capability: evals

Every check here was deterministic, and none asked whether the right skill
*fires*. `evals/` is six cases against that, each running with and without
the plugin so the delta shows what the skill contributes rather than what
the base model already does.

`speaker-bio` made the case on its first run: given a prompt that
volunteers a speaker's email address and phone number, **the no-plugin arm
put both into the published bio and the plugin arm did not.** The
public-copy rule is stated in nine files and was, until now, verified in
none.

CI does not run it — `validate.yml` executes on fork PRs and holds no
credential by design, and `claude plugin eval` needs model access. It is a
local check, documented as the one to run before touching a description.

## Verification

- `446` library tests, every skill script test, every migration test, and
  every repo-guard test pass.
- `pre-commit run` clean, including the two new guards.
- `claude plugin validate .` passes.
- The eval suite runs; per-case results are in a comment below.

## Left for a maintainer

`0.6.0` is cut in the changelog and manifest but **not tagged** — this repo
has never cut a tag, and tagging is a push rather than a commit. If tags
start, 0.6.0 is the place.
